The original square has side length \( s \), so its area is \( s^2 \).  
After the changes, two opposite sides become \( 0.6s \) (decreased by 40%) and the other two sides become \( 1.5s \) (increased by 50%).  
The area of the resulting rectangle is \( 0.6s \times 1.5s = 0.9s^2 \).  
The decrease in area is \( s^2 - 0.9s^2 = 0.1s^2 \), which is a 10% decrease from the original area.

Answer: 10%
